newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA sees consumer confidence rising late 97.
newsitem.headline: CBA sees consumer confidence rising late 97.

text.p: Australia's largest credit card issuer and home mortgage lender said on Sunday its internal data on credit card and mortgage repayments showed consumer confidence would imprvove later this year or early next year.

"There are some indications in our system that suggest that there will be a pickup in consumer confidence later this year, early next year," Commonwealth Bank Managing Director David Murray told the Nine Network's Business Sunday television programme.
"We're seeing a propensity to repay credit card debt and more importantly, a lot of poeple are paying more off their mortgages than they have to under their contracts," Murray said.
Consumer confidence has stubbornly refused to pick up this year despite five cuts in the official cash interest rate in the last 13 months to five percent.
The most widely-recognised survey of consumer confidence, the Westpac-Melbourne Institute index of consumer sentiment, rose 0.2 percent in August.
Westpac said this was disappointing as the survey was taken one week after the most recent 0.5 percentage point cut in official interest rates.
The index has actually fallen 7.8 percent since January, despite two rate cuts in that time.
Economists say employment concerns have held consumer confidence down and until the flat employment market recovers, confidence will struggle to rebound.
